_comment: Controlled vocabulary for per-scene SFX placement. The scene planner LLM picks one of the keys below as `sfx_hint` on each scene; the assemble step looks up the entry, picks a real file from `folder` (narrowed by `filename_match` if present), and places it on the timeline using the `placement` mode. Adding a hint = add an entry here. Removing a folder = update or delete entries that point to it. The `label` field is the human-readable marker shown on the timeline track in the editor.

tension_riser.label: RISER
tension_riser.description: Long swelling drone or build-up that escalates tension before a reveal. Use sparingly — at most once per video, on a build → climax transition. Pairs naturally with hook or build → climax pivots.

bass_drop_impact.label: BASS DROP
bass_drop_impact.description: Single deep bass impact — the heaviest sting available. Use ONCE per video, on the climax scene only, on the hardest emotional beat. Never on a build scene; never twice.

cinematic_hit.label: HIT
cinematic_hit.description: Mid-weight cinematic stinger for a strong revelation that isn't the final climax. Use on a major reveal in the build section, or as a softer climax alternative when bass_drop_impact would be too much.

whoosh_transition.label: WHOOSH
whoosh_transition.description: Quick whoosh marking a hard cut between scenes. Use sparingly — at most once every 3 scenes — or it loses impact. Best on perspective shifts (zoom out, jump cut to a new angle, time skip).

rocket_whoosh.label: ROCKET
rocket_whoosh.description: Heavier, longer whoosh with momentum. Use for forward motion, escalation, or 'launching into something' beats. More dramatic than whoosh_transition.

heartbeat_pulse.label: HEARTBEAT
heartbeat_pulse.description: Steady human heartbeat looping under the scene. Use during moments of intimate fear, tension, or vulnerability. Plays for the full scene duration. Most powerful when the scene is short (3-6s).

clock_tick.label: CLOCK
clock_tick.description: Quiet ticking clock under the scene. Use during scenes about time, memory, waiting, deadlines, or 'meanwhile…' beats. Plays for the full scene duration.

thinking_pad.label: THINK
thinking_pad.description: Soft 'hmm' / contemplative pad. Use during reflection, internal monologue, or 'consider this…' moments. Plays for the full scene duration.

magic_shimmer.label: SHIMMER
magic_shimmer.description: Soft sparkle / chime / 'aha moment' shimmer. Use on insights, realizations, idea-having, or 'something beautiful is happening' beats. Light and brief.

money_sting.label: MONEY
money_sting.description: Coin / cash register / value-related ding. Use ONLY on scenes literally about money, wealth, cost, or value. Never decorative.

glass_shatter.label: GLASS
glass_shatter.description: Sharp, harsh impact suitable for shattering, breaking, or violent rupture. Use on a single moment — a betrayal, a shattering belief, a violent revelation. Maximum once per video.

gunshot_punctuation.label: GUNSHOT
gunshot_punctuation.description: Single sharp punctuation mark. Use on violence, sudden death, or extremely abrupt narrative breaks. Use only when the script explicitly references such a moment — never decoratively.

rain_ambience.label: RAIN
rain_ambience.description: Rain or thunderstorm bed under the scene. Use for melancholy, isolation, contemplation, or scenes literally set in bad weather. Plays for the full scene duration.

nature_ambience.label: NATURE
nature_ambience.description: Birdsong, footsteps in grass, calm outdoor textures. Use for peaceful, wholesome, or rural scenes. Plays for the full scene duration.

crowd_cheer.label: CHEER
crowd_cheer.description: Crowd applause / cheering / stadium energy. Use on triumph, victory, recognition, or shared joy beats. One-shot, not looped.

crowd_laugh.label: LAUGH
crowd_laugh.description: Audible group laughter — sitcom-style. Use ONLY on comedic relief beats or punchlines. Never on dramatic/serious content; the tonal mismatch is jarring.

camera_shutter.label: SHUTTER
camera_shutter.description: Camera shutter / photo snap. Use on 'a moment captured', evidence reveals, photographic memory beats, or paparazzi/surveillance scenes.

keyboard_typing.label: TYPING
keyboard_typing.description: Keyboard / typewriter typing texture. Use on scenes about writing, coding, messaging, or research montages. Plays for the full scene duration.

telephone_ring.label: PHONE
telephone_ring.description: Telephone ring or dial tone. Use ONLY when the scene literally involves a phone call. Never decorative.

glitch_distort.label: GLITCH
glitch_distort.description: Digital glitch / corruption / reality-tear sound. Use on jarring transitions, system breakdowns, surreal pivots, or 'something is wrong' beats. Sharp and disorienting on purpose.

viscous_liquid.label: VISCOUS
viscous_liquid.description: Slow gloopy liquid texture. Use on body horror, dread, things-going-wrong slow burns, or unsettling slow-motion beats. Loops under the scene.

notification_ding.label: DING
notification_ding.description: UI notification / alert / 'message received' ding. Use on social-media beats, alarm beats, or 'something just happened' attention-grabs. Modern and short-form-native.

click_confirm.label: CLICK
click_confirm.description: Sharp UI click / 'correct answer' / 'done' click. Use on confirmation beats, list items being checked off, decision-made moments. Subtle and structural.

cartoon_pop.label: POP
cartoon_pop.description: Light cartoon pop / boing / appearance sound. Use ONLY on comedic or playful content; tonally wrong for drama, philosophy, or true crime.

text_appear.label: TEXT IN
text_appear.description: Short bright accent marking the moment a text overlay appears on screen. Use ONLY on text-type scenes (scene.type == 'text') — never on image/video scenes. Pairs with the visual pop animation. Keep it gentle: it should support the text reveal, not compete with it. At most one per text scene. Files for this hint live in the dedicated text_scene folder — drop your preferred 'text in' sounds there (any files matching the pattern below).

text_disappear.label: TEXT OUT
text_disappear.description: Soft sweep marking the moment a text overlay leaves the screen. Use ONLY on text-type scenes (scene.type == 'text') — never on image/video scenes. Should be airy and brief, the audio equivalent of a fade. Pairs with text_appear at the start of the same scene; using one without the other is fine. Files for this hint live in the dedicated text_scene folder — drop your preferred 'text out' sounds there (any files matching the pattern below).

text_emphasis.label: TEXT HIT
text_emphasis.description: Subtle ding/chime that lands on the emphasized word inside a text scene. Use ONLY on hook text scenes where one word is highlighted/animated (scene.type == 'text' AND a hook animation is present). Pairs with the visual emphasis beat. Use sparingly — at most once per text scene, and not on every text scene. Files for this hint live in the dedicated text_scene folder — drop your preferred 'emphasis hit' sounds there (any files matching the pattern below).

silence.label: — SILENCE —
silence.description: Explicit silence — render no SFX on this scene. Use when the absence of sound is itself the effect (a beat of stillness, a held breath before a reveal). Different from leaving sfx_hint null: this is a deliberate creative choice to suppress any ambient/auto SFX during this scene window.
